{{Short description|Stochastic diffusion process in probability theory}}
In [[probability theory]], a '''McKean–Vlasov process''' is a [[stochastic process]] described by a [[stochastic differential equation]] where the coefficients of the [[Diffusion equation|diffusion]] depend on the distribution of the solution itself.<ref>{{cite thesis | url = http://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/docs/00/65/87/66/PDF/tachet.pdf | title = Non-parametric model calibration in finance: Calibration non paramétrique de modèles en finance | first = Rémi Tachet | last = Des Combes |type=Doctoral dissertation| year = 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120511054130/http://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/docs/00/65/87/66/PDF/tachet.pdf | archive-date = 2012-05-11 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Funaki | first1 = T. | title = A certain class of diffusion processes associated with nonlinear parabolic equations | doi = 10.1007/BF00535008 | journal = Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete| volume = 67 | issue = 3 | pages = 331–348 | year = 1984 | s2cid = 121117634 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The equations are a model for [[Vlasov equation]] and were first studied by [[Henry McKean]] in 1966.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |title=A Class of Markov Processes Associated with Nonlinear Parabolic Equations |first=H. P. |last=McKean |author-link=Henry McKean |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA]] |year=1966 |volume=56 |issue=6 |pages=1907–1911 |doi=10.1073/pnas.56.6.1907 |pmid=16591437 |pmc=220210|bibcode=1966PNAS...56.1907M |doi-access=free }}</ref> It is an example of '''propagation of chaos''', in that it can be obtained as a limit of a mean-field system of interacting particles: as the number of particles tends to infinity, the interactions between any single particle and the rest of the pool will only depend on the particle itself.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Chaintron |first1=Louis-Pierre |last2=Diez |first2=Antoine |date=2022 |title=Propagation of chaos: A review of models, methods and applications. I. Models and methods |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.3934/krm.2022017 |journal=Kinetic and Related Models |volume=15 |issue=6 |pages=895 |doi=10.3934/krm.2022017 |issn=1937-5093|arxiv=2203.00446 }}</ref>

== Definition ==
Consider a measurable function <math>\sigma:\R^d \times \mathcal{P}(\R^d)\to \mathcal{M}_{d}(\R)</math> where <math>\mathcal{P}(\R^d)</math> is the space of [[Probability distribution|probability distributions]] on <math>\R^d</math> equipped with the [[Wasserstein metric]] <math>W_2</math> and <math>\mathcal{M}_{d}(\R)</math> is the space of [[Matrix (mathematics)|square matrices]] of dimension <math>d</math>. Consider a measurable function <math>b:\R^d\times \mathcal{P}(\R^d)\to \R^d</math>. Define <math>a(x,\mu) := \sigma(x,\mu)\sigma(x,\mu)^T</math>.

A stochastic process <math>(X_t)_{t\geq 0}</math> is a McKean–Vlasov process if it solves the following system:<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

* <math>X_0</math> has law <math>f_0</math>
* <math>dX_t = \sigma(X_t, \mu_t) dB_t + b(X_t, \mu_t) dt</math>

where <math>\mu_t = \mathcal{L}(X_t)</math> describes the [[Law (stochastic processes)|law]] of <math>X</math> and <math>B_t</math> denotes a <math>d</math>-dimensional [[Wiener process]]. This process is non-linear, in the sense that the associated [[Fokker–Planck equation]] for <math>\mu_t</math> is a non-linear [[partial differential equation]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

== Existence of a solution ==
The following Theorem can be found in.<ref name=":3" />

{{Math theorem
| math_statement = Suppose <math>b</math> and <math>\sigma</math> are [[Lipschitz continuity|globally Lipschitz]], that is, there exists a constant <math>C>0</math> such that:

<math>|b(x,\mu)-b(y,\nu)| + |\sigma(x,\mu)-\sigma(y,\nu)| \leq C(|x-y|+W_2(\mu,\nu))</math>

where <math>W_2</math> is the [[Wasserstein metric]].

Suppose <math>f_0</math> has finite variance.

Then for any <math>T>0</math> there is a unique strong solution to the McKean-Vlasov system of equations on <math>[0,T]</math>. Furthermore, its law is the unique solution to the non-linear [[Fokker–Planck equation]]:

<math>\partial_t \mu_t(x) = -\nabla \cdot \{b(x,\mu_t)\mu_t\} + \frac{1}{2}\sum\limits_{i,j=1}^d \partial_{x_i}\partial_{x_j}\{a_{ij}(x,\mu_t)\mu_t\}</math>
| name = Existence of a solution
}}

== Propagation of chaos ==
The McKean-Vlasov process is an example of '''propagation of chaos'''.<ref name=":3" /> What this means is that many McKean-Vlasov process can be obtained as the limit of discrete systems of stochastic differential equations <math>(X_t^i)_{1\leq i\leq N}</math>.

Formally, define <math>(X^i)_{1\leq i\leq N}</math> to be the <math>d</math>-dimensional solutions to:

* <math>(X_0^i)_{1\leq i\leq N}</math> are i.i.d with law <math>f_0</math>
* <math>dX_t^i = \sigma(X_t^i, \mu_{X_t}) dB_t^i + b(X_t^i, \mu_{X_t}) dt</math>

where the <math>(B^i)_{1\leq i\leq N}</math> are i.i.d [[Brownian motion]], and <math>\mu_{X_t}</math> is the [[empirical measure]] associated with <math>X_t</math> defined by <math>\mu_{X_t} := \frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{1\leq i\leq N} \delta_{X_t^i}</math> where <math>\delta</math> is the [[Dirac measure]].

Propagation of chaos is the property that, as the number of particles <math>N\to +\infty</math>, the interaction between any two particles vanishes, and the random empirical measure <math>\mu_{X_t}</math> is replaced by the deterministic distribution <math>\mu_t</math>. 

Under some regularity conditions,<ref name=":3" /> the mean-field process just defined will converge to the corresponding McKean-Vlasov process.

* [[Mean-field theory]]
* [[Mean-field game theory]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Carmona |first1=Rene |last2=Delarue |first2=Francois |last3=Lachapelle |first3=Aime |title=Control of McKean-Vlasov Dynamics versus Mean Field Games |url=https://carmona.princeton.edu/download/mfg/cdl.pdf |website=Princeton University}}</ref>
* [[Random matrices]]: including Dyson's model on eigenvalue dynamics for random symmetric matrices and the [[Wigner semicircle distribution]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Chan |first=Terence |date=January 1994 |title=Dynamics of the McKean-Vlasov Equation |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=22 |issue=1 |pages=431–441 |doi=10.1214/aop/1176988866 |issn=0091-1798|doi-access=free }}</ref>
